_readme: All tunable game numbers. Distances in metres, speeds in m/s, masses in kg, fuel in litres (1 L = 1 kg), thrust in kgf (1 = 9.81 N), times in seconds, money in $. Change a value, save, and the dev server reloads the game.

payloads._note: Total mass (kg) of the root slot for each payload. Heavier payloads need a bigger rocket.

fuelTypes._note: Per fuel: kg per litre (a tank holds parts.FUEL_TANK.fuelLiters), and multipliers on a booster's efficiency (isp) and push (thrust) while it burns this fuel. COLD_GAS only feeds RCS thrusters. unlockCost: one-time price to unlock the fuel in the lab (0 = open from the start).

rcs._note: Per RCS thruster, once its shell has separated: turning torque, sideways push (m/s^2) and cold gas burned per second at full steer. Boosters cannot steer in space.

rockBelt._note: The rock belt (src/modules/rockBelt). Rocks spawn ahead of the rocket across its whole view plus a margin, so it can't be flown around. Throttle timing and sideways dodges (A / D, stronger with each open RCS) avoid them. A small rock costs health; a boulder knocks off the part it hits. Each launch time picks a difficulty (timeOfDay → rockDifficulty).

dodge._note: Inside the belt A / D slide the rocket straight sideways (no leaning) and it stops when you let go. Every rocket gets the base; each open RCS (shell off, cold gas left) adds more.

difficulty._note: Per rating (1 easy … 5 hardest): rocks per 100 m climbed, share of boulders, fastest sideways drift (m/s), biggest small rock and boulder radius (m), health a small rock costs, near-miss distance (m from the hull).

camera._note: No zooming during the climb: the launch view's scale is kept the whole way up.

objectiveBonus._note: Extra share of the objective payout: no part lost in flight, and a cheap rocket.

hazards._note: Switch: with enabled=false no hazard strikes (neither on the way up nor on the Moon landing) until they are tuned. Trouble on the way to the Moon (flights with a chosen payload). At each altitude (m above Earth) the dice roll: with chance `chance` one hazard from that band's list strikes. The seed comes from the flight, so every flight differs.

challenges._note: The five flight challenges in src/modules/. Heights are metres above the pad (the Moon's pull starts near 4800 straight up). Each one has its own switch.

maxQ._note: Peak air pressure on the climb. Above `limit` (Pa) the airframe strains: health drops at damagePerSecond times the overshoot share. Throttle down to stay under it.

windShear._note: A gust layer that swings from one side to the other (m/s, scaled by the launch time's wind). Tilting past maxTiltDegrees costs damagePerSecond.

stagingFault._note: The first shell separation of a flight can jam (chance). Tap its key `taps` more times within timeLimit seconds, or the bolts blow and cost `damage` health.

radiationBelt._note: Charged particles fry the electronics: readouts glitch and health drops at dosePerSecond (crew ships take crewFactor times more). Cross it fast.

transLunarBurn._note: Aim the coast so the Moon pass (predicted low point, m) lands between lowPeriapsis and highPeriapsis. Off course at the Moon's pull, an automatic correction burn fixes it for fuel (correctionPenalty times what a clean burn would cost, at most maxCorrection m/s).

hull._note: Hull integrity is 100 at launch; every part knocked or snapped off costs perPart. At 0 the flight is lost.

orbit._goal: Enter the Moon's gravity and settle into a stable orbit.

satellite._note: Ejection: the satellite is pushed ahead and the spent stage backs off (m/s along the orbit); time speeds up so they visibly part.

rover._goal: Survive the problems in orbit, then drop the rover into the target zone.

STUCK_THRUSTER._note: Spin acceleration from the stuck thruster (deg/s²); fail if spinning faster than maxSpinDegPerSec for graceSeconds.

ORBIT_DECAY._note: A drag-like pull against your direction of travel (m/s²).

landing._goal: Bring the crew down onto the landing site, upright and gently.

launchVerdict._note: Fuel left (as delta-v, m/s) on reaching the Moon's pull in the pre-launch test flight.
